reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous pattern recognition with rigorous external explainability tools to identify shared spurious features. Autonomous analysis helps detect surface-level commonalities across instances, while XAI tools provide quantified, model-internal attribution scores to confirm spurious influence. This combination increases confidence in identifying features that are correlated in the data but semantically unrelated to the target label.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 31254) and assess whether any feature is consistently present across all instances regardless of value differences.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three instances, including their values and frequency

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse or occupation=Husband) has a plausible spurious correlation with the >50K class despite lacking semantic relevance, especially given that the true labels are unknown and the model incorrectly predicts >50K.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned hypothesis about a spurious feature that may be driving incorrect predictions due to co-occurrence in misclassified instances

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a robust, interpretable feature attribution score that can identify which features have high influence on predictions across all instances, especially in the intersection of misclassified samples. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations to validate the model's reliance on specific features. Sensitivity analysis tests whether removing a feature changes the prediction, helping isolate spurious dependencies. Together, these tools detect both high-importance and non-semantic features that may be driving misclassification.
